sources.title: Efficient Weak Signals Acquisition Strategy for GNSS Receivers
sources.venue: IEICE Transactions on Communications E99.B(1), 288-295; DOI 10.1587/transcom.2015EBP3114
sources.publication_status: journal article record verified on publisher-hosted J-STAGE page; peer-review status not independently verified
sources.access_level: publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata accessible; page states journal restricted access; full text not inspected
sources.content_locator: J-STAGE article page lines 35-47, 71-74: double-dwell approach based on periodic spread-spectrum code; conventional threshold verification can extend mean acquisition time amid noise/interference; abstract reports theoretical/simulation comparison. The reported numerical benefit is GNSS-specific and is not transferred here.

findings.claim: A staged screen/verification policy is a distinct acquisition design option worth measuring where an exploitable persistence or signal-structure cue exists: conventional threshold-based verification can spend extra time resolving false triggers, while a double-dwell scheme is studied to trade detection, false alarms, and mean acquisition time.
findings.support_locator: J-STAGE abstract, lines 71-74; article metadata/access at lines 35-47.
findings.decision_implication: Add one small matched discriminator to the eventual capture study: compare the current fixed/dwell policy with a two-stage early screen followed by confirmation, reporting time to first qualifying frequency estimate, missed/false publications, and total observation time on identical tone-present and absent-tone streams. Preserve every nonpublication and use the same false-publication criterion. Do not import the paper's claimed seconds saved or C/N0 performance.
findings.assumptions: The helper stream may offer stable structure across sequential looks that can support a confirmation rule; each look can be evaluated without changing frequency-only authority.
findings.applicability_gap: The source's scheme relies on periodic spread-spectrum code structure, while this task concerns a generated helper tone and current excerpts do not establish an analogous cue or threshold-verification workflow. It provides a design/validation lead, not evidence that double-dwell works here.
findings.next_discriminator: On matched synthetic captures, compare a single fixed confirmation interval against an early-look-plus-confirmation schedule, using tone-present and absent controls under the same offsets, reference levels, chunk partitions, and total deadline. Include false admissions and median/tail time-to-publication; inspect whether any gain survives payload/auxiliary activity.
findings.incremental_vs_seed: Seed findings cover error tails, block versus phase-difference estimators, lag/range tradeoffs, and stationary versus time-varying mismatch. They do not identify sequential staged confirmation or mean time-to-acquisition as a design discriminator. The added paper makes that small validation comparison concrete, while its GNSS-specific periodic-code mechanism limits transfer.

rejected_or_redundant.item: GNSS coherent/noncoherent integration papers and CFAR variants
rejected_or_redundant.reason: Related first-party abstracts discuss detection probability and false alarm but mostly restate seed requirements for absent-tone controls and dwell-vs-sensitivity tradeoffs; no distinct additional claim was established within this bounded continuation.

unresolved: Whether the helper acquisition path has sequential looks, threshold verification, or a temporal cue that can support a staged confirmation scheme; source excerpts do not establish this runtime behavior.

Whether staging improves time-to-frequency-publication at a controlled false-publication rate for this non-GNSS signal. The new paper's mechanism and numeric findings are specific to spread-spectrum GNSS and remain untransferred.

The existing seed uncertainties remain: threshold-tail behavior at the receiver's actual noise/activity conditions; whether chunk delivery preserves phase; estimator performance under drift/amplitude mismatch; and feasibility of the invented 0.10-Hz/6-s/95% target.
stop_reason: Sufficient incremental validation evidence found from one first-party source. Stopped after 10 logical operations (8 search queries, 2 opens, including 1 failed open); 6 of 16 total operations and 8 of 10 source opens remained; the 8-query search allowance was exhausted. No useful primary evidence was recovered for the sequential DFT lead. Completed within the 12-minute target.
escalation_ready: Yes. Retain the seed's four substantive cautions and do not treat the proposed metrics as observations. The only increment is a staged-confirmation versus fixed-dwell discriminator measuring both false admissions and time-to-frequency-publication; applicability is uncertain because the cited method exploits GNSS code periodicity. No estimator or architecture selected.
retained_seed_summary: Seed evidence (S1-S5; discovery packet r842) supports threshold/outlier caution beyond CRB or finite reported uncertainty, a simple block/DFT baseline, differential-phase delay tradeoffs, and possible degradation under time variation. Source-checks note that peer review was not independently established for those records; accessible material ranges from index abstract and institutional abstract to IEEE abstract/metadata and repository abstract, and publisher/open failures are recorded in seed_operations. Seed applicability remains model-limited: complex sinusoid/AWGN and a Doppler-spread model do not establish behavior for this receiver. Keep the original discriminator set: matched block-vs-phase comparison, lag/reset/chunk controls, stationary vs drifted captures, error tails, absent-tone false admissions, and no phase/payload authority inference.
